sentences.text: An application is filed under Section 497 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, for interim custody of two mobile phones involved in Crime No.780/2024 of Kalady Police Station.

The learned Magistrate dismissed the same, stating that in connection with the case,
a Cyber Forensic examination is necessary.

It will be better to extract the relevant portion of the above order:
"5. Report filed stating that the accused/petitioners defrauded the informant and got Rs. 19,64,461/-(Rupees Nineteen Lakh Sixty Four Thousand Four Hundred and Sixty One only) transferred to the account no 50100658670143 maintained by the 1st petitioner in HDFC bank, which is entrusted to the 2 nd petitioner.
In connection with the case, their mobile phones are seized and produced before the court.
The prosecution has objected to the release of the mobile phone on the ground that it is required for forensic examination and also on the ground of committing a similar offence.
6. The offence alleged is u/ss. 406, 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
For 2025:KER:39842 CRL.REV.PET NO.221 OF 2025 the just and fair disposal of the case, it is essential to collect all possible evidence which could be gathered.
The mobile phones are an integral part of the case.
The prosecution has already reported that they intend to send the mobile phones for forensic examination to retrieve relevant data.
Forwarding note filed.
The investigation in this case is still going on.

That being so, I am of the view that the mobile phones are essential for the ongoing investigation and hence this petition stands dismissed in the interest of justice."
2.
I see no reason to interfere with the same.

After examination of the mobile phones, the petitioners can approach the Court with a fresh application, and if such an application is filed, the Jurisdictional Court will do the needful in accordance with law.
